O.outcome_detail: User experience ratings across six UEQ categories; all category means were above the positive-evaluation threshold of 0.8.

cells.quote: All 6 UEQ categories were positively evaluated. Attractiveness (mean 2.064, SD 0.672) and stimulation (mean 1.827, SD 0.949) were the highest-rated categories, whereas dependability was the lowest-rated category (mean 1.115, SD 0.740; Figure 1).
cells.note: Single-group formative usability evaluation; the study reports descriptive UEQ ratings rather than an experimental comparison or printed effect size.

cells.quote: "The HFS group rated the training as more supportive, easy, efficient, and clear than did the VR group. No significant differences were detected between the groups in terms of excitement, interest, inventiveness, or being cutting-edge. All items had scores above 5"
cells.note: The exact item-level usability sentence is reported in the wiki entry rather than the study text reproduced above; the study text identifies the UEQ-S as the usability measure and states that both groups scored above 5 on all items.

cells.quote: "On the contrary, Perspicuity, the usability aspect how easy to learn Jupyter, appears as a dimension with the weakest personal aﬀective attitude."
cells.note: The study text supplied here does not report a numerical effect size or describe the benchmark comparison; the quote is reproduced from the wiki entry.

cells.quote: The authors report Perspicuity, "the usability aspect how easy to learn Jupyter", as the dimension with the weakest personal affective attitude, with very similar below-average impression for overall Attractiveness.
cells.note: The supplied study excerpt does not include the numerical UEQ results or describe the benchmark comparison; the quote is reproduced from the wiki entry.
